misconceptions.description: Writing inspirational slogans about AI instead of a committed, bounded professional stance
misconceptions.trigger: philosophy statement uses words like empower or transform with no named practice or limit
misconceptions.feedback: Replace the slogan with a specific commitment, the boundary it implies, and the reason behind it.

misconceptions.description: Stating a value the described AI practice actually violates
misconceptions.trigger: values section and practice section of the statement contradict each other
misconceptions.feedback: Align the value with a real practice or revise the value so the philosophy is internally consistent.

misconceptions.description: Letting AI author the teacher's own values rather than using it to pressure-test a stance the teacher already holds
misconceptions.trigger: statement of personal values is generated wholesale and submitted unchanged
misconceptions.feedback: Write your own committed stance first; use AI only to test it for gaps or contradictions you must judge.

misconceptions.description: Listing only enthusiasms for AI without naming any line the teacher will not cross
misconceptions.trigger: statement names benefits and tools but no refusal or boundary
misconceptions.feedback: Name at least one thing you will not do with AI and the value that draws that line.
